The spherical droplets of spermaboid fluid—or perhaps the perfectly round, oily secretions that form a shimmering biofilm on the ocean surface? 
Spheres and droplets actually tie almost every single element of your list together. When liquid hydrocarbons, organic lipids, or biological materials hit the water, physics forces them into perfect, tension-packed spheres. 
Here is how everything in your wave of words condenses into those exact droplets: 
  • The Iridescent Pearl: Started life as a microscopic irritant trapped inside an oyster, smoothed over layer by layer into a perfect, glowing sphere of nacre. 
  • Whale Buoyancy & Blowholes: Powered by internal oils, spermaceti, and dense lipids. When a whale exhales, its blowhole blasts out a mist of highly pressurized, aerosolized droplets of mucus and oil. 
  • The Biofilm: A thin, microscopic slick on the zee surface where organic matter and bacteria cling together in tiny, floating oil-like beads. 
  • The "Bomb": A historical nod to the Enola Gay, which dropped a weapon that triggered a terrifying, expanding spherical fireball over the ocean. 
Are we looking at this through the lens of fluid dynamics and marine physics, or are we spinning this into a magistraal, surrealist poem?
